_fields.tenant: the employer as the tracker spells it
_fields.evidence: posting | form | board_wide | rejection_mail | confirmation_page - WHERE the policy was discovered, which is often the point, because a bar that only appears on the form cannot be found by reading the posting
_fields.learned: the date the policy was established
_fields.detail: the sentence or observation it rests on, quoted rather than summarised

tenants.detail: FIXTURE ENTRY, and the case where only the rejection reveals the bar: the posting was silent and said nothing a hard-bar screen could match, so the bar was learned from the answer to the application itself. A rejection is evidence about the TENANT, not only about the application it answered, so it changes what every future round does here.

FIXTURE ENTRY. The bar was in the APPLICATION FORM while the posting read clean, and its sibling requisitions share the same federal-contract business, so the tenant is a skip rather than a per-requisition one. This is the expensive kind: it is only discovered after a resume has been tailored and a form opened.

FIXTURE ENTRY. A company-wide bar stated in a form of words containing neither 'sponsor' nor 'clearance', which is why a screen tuned to those two words passed it. Board-wide evidence means no requisition on this board is worth a tailoring cycle.
FIXTURE ENTRY. The no-sponsorship family in its own wording, in the description text rather than in a requirements heading. Recorded per tenant because every requisition on the board carries it.

FIXTURE ENTRY. An italicised note inside the description, below the responsibilities - the reading is the SENTENCE, not the keyword, so the note is quoted in full here rather than reduced to 'no sponsorship'.

FIXTURE ENTRY. The bar is phrased as the affirmative-negative: not eligible for new sponsorship, while existing transfers may be sponsored. The narrower claim is the one that matters, so the entry records the wording rather than the outcome.

FIXTURE ENTRY. Stated in the requirements list, in a sentence that also describes the role's on-site expectations - recorded as a policy because it decides whether the board is worth tailoring for, not only whether one posting is.

FIXTURE ENTRY. A defence-adjacent employer whose requirements state a status the candidate does not hold. Skipped at screening rather than argued with at Submit: the requirement is the employer's to set and the answer is a fact about the candidate.

_see_also: data/form_specs/tenant_caps.json holds the application caps, and is the file the preflight actually reads. Caps live there and nowhere else: two sources for one number is how the number drifts. This file holds the policies that are decisions - skip, no_sponsorship, form_only_bar.
